subject: Real time Chat service for stan

messages.author: b79797e24887c6c2
messages.subject: Real time Chat service for stan
parts:
Hi,
I am a beginner in stan and generally in bayesian statistics and I have to say I love it.
I was wondering if anyone had any interest in using a real time chatting service. There are several chatting platforms such as IRC, Slack, Gitter...
I usually use Gitter as it is an easy way to ask dev about PR for github repos.
I also see another advantage as there is currently to my knowledge no gitter channel about bayesian statistic.
Generally, I believe chat could be another mean of communication that would allow to answer quick dev questions as well as statistical question that do not requires in depth answer.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real time Chat service for stan
parts:
Hi Marc,

I'd encourage you to set it up. If it's useful, then great!

I'll just let you know that I am not interested in it. I prefer there to be some thought and effort into questions. That said, I understand the value of having real-time chat, so by all means, please feel free to create it.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real time Chat service for stan
parts:
Thanks for getting involved. As Daniel says, we never
know what's going to work until we try it.

I personally find real-time chat a big distraction. But
I've been known to change my mind on this kind of thing.
The more I get pushed into management and out of coding,
the more it makes sense.

So far, I've resisted all requests to install IRT, slack,
gitter, trello, or anything else that demands attention.

I'm grudgingly going along with the web-based Discourse
thing that someone else set up for stan dev discussions, but
I preferred Google Groups because it worked better through
email.

- Bob
